objective.statement: Know the signs and words that tell you how loudly to play.
successCriteria: I know p means quiet and f means loud.
I know m means moderately and doubling the letter means very.
I know crescendo means getting louder and diminuendo getting quieter.

explanation.text: Dynamics tell the player how loudly or quietly to play. They use letters taken from Italian words: p is piano (quiet) and f is forte (loud).

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets marked p, mp, mf and f, getting louder.

explanation.caption: p (quiet), mp (moderately quiet), mf (moderately loud), f (loud).

explanation.text: An m stands for mezzo, which means moderately. mp is moderately quiet and mf is moderately loud. Doubling a letter makes it stronger: pp is very quiet (pianissimo) and ff is very loud (fortissimo).
Words can change the volume gradually. Crescendo (cresc.) means getting gradually louder. Diminuendo (dim.) or decrescendo (decresc.) means getting gradually quieter.
From quietest to loudest: pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff.

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets marked pp, p, f and ff, getting louder.

steps: Look at the marks below the notes: pp, p, f, ff.
Read them in order from quiet to loud.
Which note is marked to be the loudest? The last, ff.
demonstration.textAlternative: Four notes marked from very quiet (pp) to very loud (ff).

hints: Is it about speed, volume or touch?

mistakes.wrong-category: That answer belongs to a different kind of instruction. Ask yourself: is this about speed, volume, or how the notes are played?
